threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the Overground is a ‘train’ instead of just a fancy Tube line. Locals know it's really just an extension of the bus route.
Caught the N35 last night; the driver was belting out old reggae tracks. Half the bus was singing along like a mobile concert, proper vibe.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I spotted the old lady at the bakery, arguing with the owner over the last pretzel. It felt like a scene straight outta a classic film, so local.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can grab a late-night döner after a techno club and find a spontaneous poetry slam happening by the canal. Only in Berlin.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their disdain for the BART delays—complaining about them is like our city sport. A working transplant just shrugs it off.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the 49 bus calmly eating a bowl of cereal. Only in the Tenderloin do you get such breakfast multitasking on your morning commute.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all bars close at 2 AM. The locals know the best spots keep the party going till dawn, hidden away from the tourist traps.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still expect the metro to run on time. Locals know to plan around delays like they're part of the city's charm.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think 'the tube' means a quick ride, not a gamble on whether you'll get stuck between stations for ages.
Last night on the 333, a guy pulled out a saxophone and just played Smooth Operator as we rolled past Windrush Square. Honestly, only in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a group of kids playing football in the rain, laughing like it was summer. That’s Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, you’ll find pop-up espresso bars on street corners, where baristas serve quality brews from bike carts. It's like a caffeine scavenger hunt!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: A true local knows to keep an eye on BART delays before planning a trip to the East Bay; it's like checking the weather but way more chaotic.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus with a guy serenading passengers with an out-of-tune ukulele. Only in SF do you get concert-like delays without extra fare.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists flock to Park Güell but miss the hidden gardens tucked behind Carrer de Fraternitat. That’s where the real charm lies.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell them apart by how they still ask for milk in their coffee. Locals have fully embraced the cortado.
